verdict.tagline: A masterpiece of exploration and combat, though it demands immense patience.
for_you_if: you want challenging and precise combat
you enjoy deep exploration without handholding
not_for_you_if: you dislike getting lost without clear directions
you are frustrated by long runbacks after dying

cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Early players highlight precise combat and challenging navigation alongside confusing paths and tedious runbacks.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the map and navigation lack direction, leading to confusion and getting lost without knowing where to go next.

citations.review_text: Best souls-like metroidvania I've ever played - The graphics, music and gameplay are all so good. Would recommend as long as you're ok with backtracking and feeling lost.

As an newbie indie developer, I’m always fascinated by games that make a small set of ideas feel boundless. Hollow Knight does exactly that. Its hand drawn caverns, ruined cities, and eerie soundtrack turn Hallownest into a place I want to explore even when I’m not quite sure where the path leads.

The combat is simple to learn but wonderfully precise. Every jump, slash, and dodge feels deliberate, and bosses reward patience more than button mashing. Charms let me shape my approach, while new abilities open up routes that once seemed impossible. Best of all, exploration feels genuinely rewarding. A hidden passage might lead me to a new tool, a strange character, or a story fragment that changes how I see this beautiful world of Hallownest. 

That mystery can be a double edged sword. Hallownest is huge, backtracking can be drag, and the game sometimes leaves me wondering where to go next. Its difficulty can be demanding, but its controls are fair, so failure usually feels like a lesson rather than a cheap trick.

Hollow Knight is a haunting, generous adventure built with remarkable craft. It may test my patience, but for players who love getting lost, learning a boss’s rhythm, and uncovering a world one secret at a time, makes it a special game. This is an inspiring example of what a small team can create. Thank you Team Cherry.

You play as a little guy so it's automatically a 9/10. Missing point is from the fact that you lose all your money if you die while your soul is missing. Also it really needs a journal. I don't want it to hold my hand but at least telling me what I have to do next would be nice, instead of just going about aimlessly until I encounter the next boss by accident.

Really fun, but going in blind (without knowing ANYTHING about the story or what its about) can be tough as theres always new spaces to explore opening up, and its easy to not know what to do next to progress or to get lost in the same areas. Despite that, i ABSOLUTELY reccomend this game, go play it.
cool game but i got lost A LOT

I understand why people would like this game, but I could simply never get into it. The absolute lack of direction is a starting point for me, and you will 90% of the time not know where you are going without a guide from an external source helping you. Second is the trial and error. Personally, I hate trial and error types of games, but I make exceptions for games such as Terraria, with dying to bosses multiple times. But this game tries its hardest to punish you for dying to literally anything in the game, and makes it as annoying as possible to get back to where you were. Third I'd like to mention is the platforming; I hate all platformers. That's it.

Not as polished as any proper metroidvania gameplaywise. Not as beautiful as Ori to be a fairytale. Most of the plot is done by backtracking over empty locations without any proper and covinient way to figure out where you are.
Mostly hyped by zoomers who see some "Grand Drama" behind a really hollow and shallow game

claims.claim: Reviewers describe getting lost easily and lacking clear direction on where to go next or how to find required abilities.

citations.review_text:
This game is fairly challenging and fun for what it is. It's world is beautifully drawn in its hand-drawn art style and it looks gorgeous. the platforming can be a struggle at times, but the movement feels so fluid and strings together very nicely to make you feel good about the platforming. its challenge comes from the core boss fights, but the abilities you get and upgrades make it so fun to fight. The music is also amazing, Christopher Larkin composed this and the subtle ambiance with a soothing track to accompany it is always a treat to listen to, and the heavy and intimidating songs for bosses are beautifully done.

The only issue with this game that I can think of as an actual drawback is the fact that it is a metroid-vania. The world is huge to explore with hundreds of secrets that a few that I myself haven't even known about until a few days ago and possibly more. These sound like good things, more to find. But in reality, if someone gets lost easily, doesn't understand the map, and has trouble navigating, then this game will be a little bit of a challenge in that aspect. Things are usually locked behind an ability that you will find out that you need to progress, but you have no idea where to find it. The only thing you can really do is explore, and discover every nook and cranny of the areas and leave no wall untouched. 

This game is a lot of fun and I always find myself coming back to it every couple of months or every year, and I always want to 100% it (iykyk.) I still listen to the soundtrack and always love to see my friends or others play the game for the first time and have the same reactions that I had. It's weird to me to have some kind of nostalgia for the game even though it's not that old and neither am I. But its a fun time regardless. If i had to give it a score, it would be a 9/10 or a 93/100. Thank you Team Cherry for this beautifully hand-crafted game and I can't recommend it enough to people who haven't tried it in recent years now that t…

Hollow Knight is a cool game, and I really like the platforming and the challenge, especially the difficult boss fights. However, some things frustrate me. Having to travel long distances to fight the same boss again after dying, especially when there's no fast travel nearby, can get annoying. I also don’t love feeling lost and not knowing where I’m supposed to go next. I enjoy challenging games, but I prefer when a game gives a clearer sense of direction. Overall, it's a great game, but some design choices make the experience more frustrating than it needs to be. That’s just my opinion, so don’t start crying, little 'oh, you’re so brave' guys.

Positives:

- Game is a metroidvania with a lot of personality.
- It takes elements for Souls games.
- Art is beautiful.
- Great variety of builds as you progress.

Negatives:

- Traversing can be a little tiring late into the game (this game definitely needs fast travel in more areas of the map)
- Trial of the Fool 3rd Stage is kinda idiotic... No way to heal while the floor has spikes and you have to fight airborne enemies.

I definitely recommend this game, especially because the base price is really cheap and you can get it at a much lower price with discounts. Such a great with an absolute fair price.

claims.claim: Reviewers cite the White Palace and the Path of Pain as brutally difficult platforming challenges.

citations.review_text:
Is it one of my all-time favorite games? Yes.
Was it unplayable without mods? YES.

Okay so hear me out: I know this game is supposed to be hard, but I'm someone with very little patience that can't be redoing things thousand times until I finally get it right.

I played the first one or two areas without any mods, but I kept getting lost so I looked up where to buy each map at least. But then, I was sooo annoyed by the lack of benches and how long it took to get to each place, the Benchwarp Mod saved my life. I still struggled a lot but it was managable, but at the very end I ended up having to use the Easy Mode Mod because it was simply impossible.

But my biggest problems were the plataforms, so yeah, I had to ask for my friend (shout out to Lucas!) to finish the White Palace for me lol. But I did finish the rest myself, even though I gave up on trying to beat Radiance to get the True Ending.

Despite all the struggle: I really fell in love with this game 🥲💞

The scenarios, music and characters design are all an incredible masterpiece!!! Discovering this world was simply magical to me and I hold it very close in my hear 💖

PS: I did really love some fights that kinda felt like dancing a choreography, y'know?? The Lord Mantis' & both of Hornet's were actually so enjoyable to play!!!

Do not go into path of pain, not worth it, the tower of razorblades, the white palace. Beautiful, Beautiful, white palace, will be desecrated with the blood of team cherry. I do not know what they were on when making path of pain, but let me assure you, i am already depressed as of writing this, and it did not help. I love this game but dear god, you have to do it in one sitting meaning practically no taking breaks to rest by getting off the game.
Edit: I beat path of pain, nevermind this WAS a negative review but god damn i love team cherry and i felt so accomplished after doing path of pain

remove these three things from the game:
- primal aspids
- the white palace
- the colosseum
please team cherry i get this game hasn't needed a proper update since 2022 but im not trying to fight GREAT HOPPERS in an enclosed space. :hornetyams:

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the opening hours as difficult and punishing, noting that players may feel lost without a clear sense of direction or objective initially.

citations.review_text:
Now that I've gotten all of the achievements, it felt fitting to write a review on it. I first played Hollow Knight in June 2019 on a different platform. I remember feeling frustrated and getting a little annoyed over the difficulty of the game. I shortly dropped it afterwards and didn't touch it for years. It wasn't until late 2025 that I actually managed to finish it. It took me six years to beat this game. I bring up this up to better emphasize why I recommend this game. This game is difficult, yes. The bosses hit hard, especially when you're just getting started. The winding paths makes it easy to get lost. You may die in two seconds because of explosions in Fog Canyon and lose all your money. You missed the same jump on a parkour section for the 18th time, and now you have to start over. I get it, I really do. After all, it happened to me plenty of times. This is more than enough to put off the average player. However, if you can get past the first hurdle that is this game's difficulty, you're left with something amazing.

More than anything, Hollow Knight is beautiful. The areas are all such pretty sights to behold. You explore a fallen kingdom and you discover what came of this place and what picked up the debris. There is the lush jungles of Greenpath, the enchanting melancholy you feel in the City of Tears, the dread of diving into Deepnest, and the way the whole world begins to change around you. Any good metroidvania lives by one ironclad rule: environmental storytelling. It's actually not that easy to pull off as you may thing. Hollow Knight does it exceptionally well. All of these give you an experience that will stick you long after you stop playing the game and remain a moment you can look back on happily. Then, there's the music. The music can uplifting in the face of adversity like the Soul Sanctum or be enchantingly dreary like when you reach the City of Tears. The boss themes are a masterclass of their own.

The combat is difficult to start off wi…

I started playing Hollow Knight just over a year ago, and yet I still remember that first playthrough like it was yesterday. Before Hollow Knight I was like a sheltered toddler in terms of what kind of games I played. A lot of Nintendo. Some Minecraft. A few indie games. So when I booted up Hollow Knight for the first time, I had absolutely no idea what to expect.

The first couple hours were rough. Really, really rough. I was convinced I had finally bought a game that I simply wasn't going to enjoy. The enemies were ridiculously punishing, I had absolutely no sense of direction, and there wasn't even a clear objective of where to go next.

Then, slowly, but surely, I start to get my bearings. 3 hours later, time seems to disappear and I become fully immersed in the beauty of Hallownest. Every inch of the map was something new; the game never punished you for exploring every nook and cranny. It was so rewarding, and the more I played the more I understood just how expansive the world was.

Fast forward 217 hours, and I had every achievement and had 112% completed the game four separate times, including on Steel Soul. And I loved every second of it. This game is not one to sleep on.

The soundtrack is [i]immaculate[/i]. Often times you don't even notice it and it blends in perfectly with the environment. Other times it perfectly captures the scale of a cutscene, like Sealed Vessel.

The art direction is also phenomenal. Every little detail is accounted for, and every area has something unique about it. There are few things more rewarding than sitting down at the hidden bench in Greenpath, with a beautiful waterfall in the background to accompany you. Or walking into City of Tears for the first time. Or brutally navigating your way through Deepnest on one singular mask and finding relief at an unexpected hot spring.

The progression is done incredibly well. I would by no means describe Hollow Knight as linear, yet you can still always tell when you've made…
